Vehicle Incident Report -- Emberfall Wildfire Response Contractors, Unit 14 (Crew Transport)
Date: 2026-08-03 | Filed by: Crew Lead Cyrus Beaumont

At approximately 05:50, a 12-passenger crew transport van (Unit 14) veered off a forest access road and rolled onto its side while descending a switchback grade during pre-dawn transport to a fire line assignment near Cinder Ridge. The van was being driven by Anouk Verlinden, a contract driver from Alderney Freight Systems (not an Emberfall employee) under a driver-services agreement between Emberfall and Alderney. Seven Emberfall firefighters were passengers; all were wearing seatbelts per policy.

Injuries: Two firefighters sustained minor injuries (bruising and a wrist sprain) and were treated on-site by the crew's EMT before being cleared to continue light duty; neither required transport to a hospital. Driver Verlinden sustained a laceration requiring stitches and was transported to Cinder Valley Regional Hospital by a following support vehicle; she was treated and released the same day. No fatalities.

Road conditions: The access road had recent grading work that left a soft shoulder, not marked with any warning signage at the time of the incident. Emberfall's own safety audit of this road, conducted 3 weeks prior, had flagged the shoulder condition as 'monitor, not yet urgent' -- this incident has prompted an immediate re-grading request to the Forest Service, which manages the road.

Vehicle: Unit 14 sustained body damage and a cracked windshield; it has been removed from the active fleet pending inspection. This is the first rollover incident in Emberfall's crew-transport fleet in the 6 seasons company records cover, though there was an unrelated flat-tire incident on a different unit last season with no injuries.

---
Follow-up note, 2026-08-04, from Emberfall Safety Director Perpetua Nwosu:

Per our contract with Alderney, their drivers are responsible for their own workers' comp coverage as independent contractor personnel, separate from our Emberfall crew's coverage -- so Verlinden's injury claim routes through Alderney, not through us, even though the incident happened on an Emberfall-directed transport run. Our two injured firefighters' claims route through Emberfall's standard workers' comp as expected. Root cause review is scheduled for 2026-08-10 with both companies present. Separately, Alderney has confirmed Verlinden will be placed on paid leave from her driving duties (per Alderney's own policy, not ours) until the root cause review concludes and she's cleared to return to driving assignments. Emberfall's crew, meanwhile, remains on normal duty rotation, with the two lightly injured firefighters continuing light-duty assignments as noted above.

Thackeray Cloud Foundry -- Shared Responsibility & Security Whitepaper (excerpt), reviewed by Brackenridge Assisted Living IT, 2026-03-30

Section 1: Shared Responsibility Model. Thackeray is responsible for physical data center security, network infrastructure, hypervisor security, and the underlying database engine's patching. Customers (e.g., Brackenridge) are responsible for: application-level access control configuration, data classification, encryption key management (Thackeray provides the capability; the customer must enable and configure it), and user account lifecycle management (provisioning/deprovisioning).

Section 2: Encryption. Encryption at rest is available but is opt-in, configured per-database by the customer; it is not enabled by default on new database instances. Encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+) is enforced by default and cannot be disabled.

Section 3: Compliance. Thackeray's underlying infrastructure holds SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA-eligible service designation; however, HIPAA eligibility of the infrastructure does NOT make a customer's specific use of it automatically HIPAA-compliant -- the customer must independently configure the service in a compliant manner and sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with Thackeray, which is a separate, opt-in step.

Section 4: Backups. Automated daily backups are included by default, retained for 7 days; longer retention (up to 1 year) is available as a paid add-on. Backups are encrypted regardless of whether the source database has encryption at rest enabled.

---
Q&A Appendix (from Brackenridge's follow-up call, 2026-04-02):

Q: If we don't specifically enable encryption at rest, is our resident data still encrypted at rest by some default mechanism?
A: No. Without explicitly enabling it per-database, resident data sits unencrypted at rest on our storage layer, though it is still protected by our physical and access-control safeguards.

Q: Do we need a BAA to store resident health-related data, given the platform is 'HIPAA-eligible'?
A: Yes. 'HIPAA-eligible' describes our infrastructure's capability, not your compliance status. You must sign our BAA and configure the service according to our HIPAA configuration guide before storing PHI.

Q: Has Brackenridge signed a BAA with Thackeray yet?
A: Not as of this call. Your account team has sent the BAA for signature; it is pending your legal team's review.

Q: One more -- once the BAA is signed, does that automatically enable encryption at rest for our existing databases?
A: No, those are two separate steps. Signing the BAA is a contractual step; enabling encryption at rest is a technical configuration step you'd still need to do separately in the console for each database. We'd recommend scheduling both as part of the same rollout plan so neither gets forgotten.

Ridgecrest Manufacturing -- CNC Machinist (All Levels Welcome)

We're hiring across three levels for our CNC machining floor: Apprentice, Journeyman, and Master, based on demonstrated skill and certification, not just years of tenure.

Apprentice ($19-22/hr): No prior CNC experience required; enrolled in or willing to enroll in our in-house 18-month apprenticeship program (co-op with the local community college). Must have basic shop math skills (fractions, decimals, basic geometry) -- tested during the interview.

Journeyman ($26-32/hr): Completed apprenticeship OR 3+ years of equivalent CNC experience, plus NIMS (National Institute for Metalworking Skills) credential in at least one machining area. Can set up and run jobs independently with minimal supervision.

Master ($35-42/hr): 7+ years experience, NIMS credentials in at least 3 areas, and demonstrated ability to program from blueprint without CAM software assistance for at least some job types. Master machinists also mentor apprentices as part of the role.

All levels: High school diploma/GED required. Steel-toed boots required (we provide a $150 annual boot allowance). This is a 1st-shift role (6am-2:30pm); we do not currently have 2nd or 3rd shift openings. Overtime is voluntary, not mandatory, though frequently available.

Benefits (all levels): Health/dental/vision after 60 days. 401k with 50% match up to 6% of pay. Tool allowance of $500/year for personal tool purchases (company provides all machine-specific tooling; this allowance is for personal hand tools only).

Thackeray Foods Group Foundation -- Food Security Innovation Grant -- 2026 Guidelines

1. Purpose. Supporting pilot projects that reduce food insecurity through supply chain innovation, food rescue technology, or last-mile distribution improvements.

2. Eligibility. Open to 501(c)(3) nonprofits, food banks, and food rescue organizations. Government agencies may apply but are capped at 20% of total awards this cycle (a soft cap the committee tracks, not a hard per-applicant disqualifier). For-profit food tech startups are eligible only through the separate Innovation Track (Section 7), not this general track.

3. Award Size. $20,000-$150,000. Organizations with an annual operating budget under $500,000 are capped at requesting a maximum of $50,000, to avoid overwhelming smaller organizations' financial management capacity; this cap does not apply to organizations above that budget threshold.

4. Match. No cash match required. A minimum 5% in-kind match (volunteer time, donated space) is required and must be documented in the budget narrative.

5. Timeline. Letter of inquiry (LOI) due 2026-10-01; invited full proposals due 2026-12-01; decisions by 2027-02-15.

6. Restrictions. Funds may not be used for direct food purchase (this grant funds infrastructure/technology/process innovation, not commodity purchase) or for capital construction of buildings (equipment purchases under $10,000 per item are allowed).

7. Innovation Track (For-Profit). A separate $500,000 pool is reserved for for-profit food-tech startups, structured as a below-market convertible note rather than a grant; terms are in a separate document (Appendix F) and are NOT the same as the nonprofit track described above.

---
FAQ Addendum (posted 2026-09-10, based on applicant questions):

Q: Our nonprofit's operating budget is $480,000. Can we request $65,000?
A: No. Organizations under the $500,000 budget threshold are capped at $50,000 regardless of project merit; you would need to scope the request down or wait until your operating budget exceeds the threshold in a future cycle.

Q: We are a municipal food bank (a government agency). Are we eligible?
A: Yes, government agencies are eligible, subject to the soft 20% award-pool cap the committee tracks internally -- there's no need for you to track this yourself, just apply normally.

Q: Can grant funds cover the cost of a walk-in freezer (a piece of equipment, not a building)?
A: If the freezer unit itself costs under $10,000, yes. If it requires new construction or a building addition to house it, the construction portion is not fundable, though the freezer unit purchase itself still could be, if structured as a separable line item.

Q: Is the in-kind match requirement ever waived?
A: Not for this general track. The Innovation Track (Section 7) has different terms entirely and this FAQ does not apply to it.
